summary: Wildcard dependency on author-controlled package pulls arbitrary install-time code
details: package.json declares the dependency `abbishal-poc-as-dependency` with the version range `*`, an unpinned wildcard on another package in the same author's namespace. Running `npm install tostpro` resolves and fetches the latest published version of that dependency with no version pin and no integrity constraint, and executes any lifecycle scripts (`preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`) that version ships. Whoever controls the `abbishal-poc-as-dependency` name therefore controls arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine at install time. The published tarball itself ships only `package.json` and `README.md` — the declared `main` (`dist/index.js`) is absent and no scripts block is present, so the manifest's wildcard dependency is the entire install-time surface. README self-identifies this as a dependency-confusion proof of concept.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
